lines.text: Many learners say: I have many parents in this city.
Better: I have many relatives in this city.
The second! My aunt and my cousins are my relatives.

data.wrong: I have many parents in this city.
data.right: I have many relatives in this city.

options: My aunt and my cousins are my parents.

native.tip: “Parents” são só pai e mãe. Para a família toda, use “relatives”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I have many parents in this city.” O certo é “I have many relatives in this city.” Em português “parentes” é a família toda, mas em inglês “parents” são só pai e mãe. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.

en.tip: “Parents” means only mother and father. For the whole family, use “relatives”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I have many parents in this city.” The right way is “I have many relatives in this city.” In Portuguese “parentes” means the whole family, but in English “parents” means only mother and father. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
